architecture.name: head-dim-landscape-open-models
architecture.head_dims: Landscape as of 2026-09-06, all values verified against official Hugging Face config.json files. MODAL DIM SHIFTS: 2023-2025 generation is uniformly d=128 (Qwen2.5 all sizes, Qwen3 8B/32B/30B-A3B/235B-A22B, Llama-3.1/3.3, Llama-4 Scout, Phi-4, Mistral 7B/Small-24B/Small-4-119B/Medium-3.5, MiniMax-M1/M2 softmax layers, GLM-4.5/4.6). 2025-2026 frontier generation moves the FULL-ATTENTION head dim to 256: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (head_dim 256, explicit), entire Qwen3.5 line (0.8B-122B, head_dim 256), Qwen3.6-27B/35B and Qwen3.8-27B (head_dim 256 = local anchor key_length=value_length=256; public HF configs use the field name head_dim, not key_length/value_length), Gemma-2-9B (256), Gemma-3-1B/4B/12B (256), Gemma-4 (256 base). Outliers on the small side: GPT-OSS-120B/20B use head_dim 64 (only major family below 128). Outlier above 256: Gemma-4-26B-A4B global layers use global_head_dim 512. Gemma-27B-class exceptions: Gemma-2-27B and Gemma-3-27B use head_dim 128 despite the family's 256 convention. MLA families (DeepSeek-V3/R1/V3.2, Kimi-K2, GLM-5/5.2, Kimi-K3) expose NO single head_dim; effective per-head lengths are qk 192-256 and v 128-256.
architecture.qkv_dim_divergence: Three divergence classes. (1) MLA (qk_dim != v_dim, latent-compressed): DeepSeek-V3/R1 and Kimi-K2: qk_nope_head_dim 128 + qk_rope_head_dim 64 = 192-length keys, v_head_dim 128; cached/absorbed form is key_length 576 (kv_lora_rank 512 + 64 rope) vs value_length 512. GLM-5/GLM-5.2 push divergence further: qk_nope 192 + rope 64 = 256-length keys against v_head_dim 256 (qk and v equal length but different composition), kv_lora_rank 512, q_lora_rank 2048. Kimi-K3/Kimi-Linear use the same 128+64/128 MLA on their full-attention layers. (2) Partial-RoPE splits the key dim into rotated/unrotated parts rather than qk-vs-v divergence: Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.6/3.8 partial_rotary_factor 0.25, GLM-4.5/4.6 0.5, Phi-4-mini 0.75 (LongRoPE), DeepSeek/Kimi rope fraction 64/192 = 1/3. (3) No divergence: all GQA/MHA families have key_length = value_length = head_dim (Qwen, Llama, Gemma, Phi-4, Mistral, GPT-OSS, MiniMax softmax layers).
architecture.kv_heads_gqa: GQA is universal; MHA has disappeared except within MLA latent compression. Ratios: Qwen2.5-7B 28:4 (7:1), Qwen2.5-72B 64:8, Qwen3-8B 32:8, Qwen3-32B 64:8, Qwen3-235B-A22B 64:4 (16:1), Qwen3-Next 16:2 (8:1), Qwen3.5-27B 24:4 (6:1), Qwen3.5-9B 16:4, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 16:2, Qwen3.6/3.8-27B 24:4. Llama-3.1-8B 32:8, Llama-4-Scout 40:8 (5:1). Gemma-2-9B 16:8 and Gemma-2-27B 32:16 (2:1, unusually low), Gemma-3-1B 4:1 heads with 1 KV head (near-MQA), Gemma-3-4B/12B/27B 2:1, Gemma-4-31B 32:16, Gemma-4-26B-A4B 16:8. Phi-4 40:10 (4:1), Phi-4-mini 24:8 (3:1). Mistral-7B 32:8, Mistral-Small-24B 32:8, Mistral-Small-4-119B 32:32 (full MHA in 2026, unique), Mistral-Medium-3.5 96:8 (12:1). GPT-OSS 64:8 (8:1). MiniMax-M1 64:8, MiniMax-M2 48:8. GLM-4.5/4.6 96:8 (12:1). DeepSeek-V3/R1 and Kimi-K2 set num_key_value_heads = num_attention_heads = 128 (or 64) because KV is a single shared latent (kv_lora_rank 512): MQA-like at the cache level despite nominal head counts. GLM-5.2 likewise 64:64 with latent 512.
architecture.hybrid_pattern: Linear-attention hybrids are now standard in frontier open models, all at 3:1 or 7:1 linear:full ratios. Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B: 3 Gated DeltaNet (linear) : 1 full attention, config full_attention_interval 4; linear heads are separate from attention heads: linear_num_key_heads 16 x linear_key_head_dim 128 and linear_num_value_heads 32 x linear_value_head_dim 128. Qwen3.5 (27B 64 layers, 9B/4B 32 layers, 35B-A3B 40 layers), Qwen3.6-27B/35B and Qwen3.8-27B inherit the identical 3:1 layer_types pattern (linear_attention x3, full_attention x1 repeating) with the same linear 16x128 key / 48x128 value (27B) head layout - confirming the local anchor hybrid 3:1 linear:full. Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B and Kimi-K3 (93 layers): 3 Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) : 1 MLA full, full_attn_layers [4,8,...], KDA 32 heads x head_dim 128. MiniMax-Text-01 and MiniMax-M1: 7 Lightning Attention (linear) : 1 softmax full (attn_type_list 0^7,1 repeating over 80 layers); MiniMax-M2 reverted to full attention on all 62 layers. Non-linear hybrids: Gemma-2/3/4 use 5:1 sliding_window:full (sliding_window_pattern 6, window 1024; Gemma-2 window 4096); GPT-OSS alternates sliding-window-128 and full 1:1 with learned attention sinks; Llama-4 uses iRoPE: no_rope_layers pattern drops RoPE on every 4th (global) layer while dims stay uniform; DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5/5.2 replace dense full attention with DSA sparse attention (topk 2048) plus a lightweight indexer (GLM-5: index_n_heads 32 x index_head_dim 128).
architecture.heterogeneous_dims: Two distinct per-layer divergence patterns. (1) Heterogeneous HEAD DIMS (first in any open model): Gemma-4-26B-A4B config carries head_dim 256 for the 26 sliding-window layers and a separate global_head_dim 512 for the 4 full-attention (global) layers - verified directly in the google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it config.json and documented in transformers issue #45201 ([Gemma 4] per-layer FlashAttention dispatch: FA2 for sliding layers head_dim=256, SDPA fallback for global head_dim=512 which exceeds FA2's max 256). The sibling Gemma-4-31B and Gemma-4-E4B configs show a single head_dim 256 on all layers, so 512-globals heterogeneity is currently specific to 26B-A4B. (2) Heterogeneous LAYER TYPES with uniform dims: Gemma sliding:full 5:1, GPT-OSS sliding:full 1:1, Llama-4 iRoPE no-rope every 4th layer, Qwen/Kimi/MiniMax linear:full patterns, DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM-5 DSA sparse layers. In all Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8, Kimi, MiniMax, GPT-OSS, Gemma models the head_dim itself is constant across layers of the same attention type.
architecture.hidden_derivation: The heads-derived-from-hidden convention (head_dim = hidden_size / num_attention_heads) has broken down in frontier families. STILL DERIVED (exact division): Qwen2.5 (e.g. 7B: 3584/28=128; 72B: 8192/64=128), Qwen3 dense/MoE (4096/32, 5120/64), Llama-3.1 (4096/32=128), Llama-4-Scout (5120/40=128), Phi-4 (5120/40=128, no explicit head_dim field in config), Phi-4-mini (3072/24=128), Mistral all generations (4096/32, 12288/96), Kimi-Linear wrapper-level field (2304/32=72, legacy; real attention dims are MLA/KDA). NOT DERIVED (explicit head_dim with heads*head_dim != hidden): Qwen3-Next (16x256=4096 vs hidden 2048), Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8-27B (24x256=6144 vs hidden 5120 - matches local anchor), Qwen3.5-4B (4096 vs 2560), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (4096 vs 2048; note Qwen3.5-9B 16x256=4096 equals hidden 4096 only coincidentally), Gemma-2-9B (16x256=4096 vs 3584), Gemma-2-27B (32x128=4096 vs 4608), Gemma-3-27B (32x128=4096 vs 5376; query_pre_attn_scalar 168 = hidden/heads is the scaling divisor, NOT head_dim), Gemma-3-4B/12B and 1B (8x256=2048 vs 2560, 4096 vs 3840, 1024 vs 1152), Gemma-4-31B (32x256=8192 vs 5376), GPT-OSS (64x64=4096 vs 2880), GLM-4.5/4.6 (96x128=12288 vs 5120), MiniMax-M1 (64x128=8192 vs 6144), MiniMax-M2 (48x128=6144 vs 3072), GLM-5.2 (64x256=16384 vs 6144). Consequence for kernels: head_dim must be read from config, never inferred from hidden_size/heads; Qwen3.5+ and Gemma both have q-projections larger than hidden while v/o projections match head_dim*heads.

kernel_support.supported_dims: Demand-side landscape vs kernel coverage sets: FA2 ships template instantiations for head_dim {64,128} plus 256 (Hopper forward only); SageAttention 2.0 DISPATCH_HEAD_DIM covers {64,128} only, with the maintainer stating (jason-huang03, SageAttention #47, 2024-11-24): 'there are difficulities to optmize performance other than 64,128 and 256. For head dim 256 the block size is different so we do not release this for a clean interface (I think head dim greater than 128 is quite rare)' and for other dims 'we plan to pad it to 64 or 128, just as flash attention does'. That rarity premise is now factually stale for open models: Qwen3-Next/3.5/3.6/3.8 and Gemma-2/3/4 put 256 in front-page models, Gemma-4-26B-A4B puts 512 on global layers, GPT-OSS puts 64 in an 8:1 GQA workhorse, and even image/video generation (Ideogram 4.0, per a 2026-06 comment on the same issue) uses 256. Achievable coverage sets implied by the landscape: {64,128,256} mandatory, 512 desirable via k-chunking, MLA handled separately via absorbed 576/512 or nope/rope split paths.
kernel_support.capability_gate: The head-dim landscape interacts with compute capability in two ways. First, dimension coverage gates: FA2's 256 support is Hopper-forward-only per the cross-referenced FlashAttention issues (#801: larger head dims nontrivial; #2318: head_dim 256 works on Hopper forward, 512 still unsupported), so Ampere/Ada/Turing cannot use FA2 at 256 regardless of capability. Second, sm-specific path gates: sm_75 (Turing) lacks cp.async and BF16, and FA2's sm75 support was upstreamed for the {64,128} template set - the sm_75 bridge kernel plan targets exactly the gap left between FA2's dimension ceiling (256 on Hopper only) and its sm75 floor ({64,128}). Hybrid models (Qwen3.5+ 3:1, Kimi 3:1, MiniMax 7:1) additionally gate on having any full-attention kernel at all for the 1-in-4 or 1-in-8 full layers where d=256 lives.
kernel_support.fallback_semantics: Concrete fallback behaviors observed for out-of-coverage dims: SageAttention: hard error from DISPATCH_HEAD_DIM ('Unsupported head dim') for non-{64,128}, with padding-to-64/128 planned for odd dims; HuggingFace transformers on Gemma-4-26B-A4B with attn_implementation=flash_attention_2: raises 'FlashAttention only supports head dimensions up to 256 (got head_dim=512 in layer 3 [global attention layer])', and the pragmatic workaround is dispatching FA2 on sliding layers + SDPA on global layers (issue #45201 author notes falling back to SDPA everywhere sacrifices ~87% of potential FA2 speedup); vLLM and FlashInfer reject unsupported head dims at model-load time for fixed-template backends and fall back to Triton/eager paths where generic kernels exist. For models: no silent wrong-output fallbacks documented; failures are loud at load or dispatch.
kernel_support.ci_hardware_coverage: Not directly exercised by this model-landscape item; the landscape defines what CI coverage would need to prove. Current de facto coverage: FA2 CI runs sm80/sm90 with {64,128} (+256 Hopper fwd); SageAttention CI is sm80/sm86/sm89/sm90-centric with {64,128}; transformers issue #45201 shows Gemma-4 shipped without any CI exercising per-layer heterogeneous head dims on consumer GPUs. Implication for the sm_75 plan: the d=256 model set (Qwen3.5+, Gemma-2/3/4) has zero kernel-level test coverage below sm90, and the 512-global case (Gemma-4-26B-A4B) has none anywhere outside SDPA. [uncertain - no direct CI-matrix evidence collected in this item]

performance.turing_baseline: No Turing (T4/2080Ti/RTX 6000) published benchmark numbers exist for the 2025-2026 d=256 model generation in this item's scope; none of the surveyed sources (Qwen3-Next blog, vLLM blog, HF configs, transformers/SageAttention issues) report sm_75 measurements. Related measured signal only: transformers #45201 reports the qualitative SDPA-vs-FA2 gap on Gemma-4 sliding layers (~87% of FA2 speedup lost when falling back to SDPA everywhere) on the reporter's hardware (not identified as Turing). [uncertain - no Turing-side numbers found]
performance.d256_feasibility: Model side: d=256 is not only achievable but mainstream - it is the shipped full-attention head dim of Qwen3-Next and the entire Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 line (27B: 24 heads x 256 = 6144 q-proj vs hidden 5120, 4 KV heads so KV cache per layer = 4x2x256 elements), Gemma-2/3 (256), and Gemma-4 (256, with 512 on 4 global layers of 26B-A4B). GQA keeps KV-cache cost in check: Qwen3.8-27B stores 4 KV heads x 256 = 1024 per K and V per token vs Gemma-3-27B 16x128 = 2048 - the 256-dim + low-KV-head design is KV-neutral to cheaper than 128-dim high-GQA at equal hidden size. GPT-OSS's d=64 halves per-head state and compensates with 64 heads. Kernel side: d=256 exceeds the FA2 sm75 template ceiling; feasibility on Turing requires the bridge kernel (native d=256 template or k-chunked 256 in two 128 accumulations), and 512 globals require at least chunking. Partial-RoPE models (Qwen3.6/3.8 factor 0.25) reduce per-element rope cost but do not change the attention kernel's head-dim requirement.
performance.cost_analysis: Quantified shape costs from configs. Registers/accumulators: doubling head dim 128->256 doubles the per-head QK^T and PV accumulation work per query tile (mma count doubles for the same block sizes) and pushes softmax over 256-wide scores; this is the stated reason SageAttention withholds a clean 256 interface ('block size is different'). KV-cache bytes per token per layer: Qwen3.8-27B 4 KV x 256 x 2 (K+V) x 2 bytes (BF16) = 4 KB; DeepSeek-V3 MLA latent 512+64 x 2 bytes = 1152 B regardless of 128 heads (5.7x smaller than MHA 128x192x2x2=98KB would be); GPT-OSS 8x64x2x2=2 KB; Mistral-Small-4 MHA 32x128x2x2=16 KB (worst in class); Gemma-4-31B 16x256x2x2=16 KB. Hybrid ratios cut full-attention KV layers by 4x (Qwen3.5/Kimi 3:1) or 8x (MiniMax 7:1), so only the 1-in-4 full layers at d=256 contribute decode attention state - e.g. Qwen3.8-27B effectively pays full-attention KV on 16 of 64 layers. Chunking overhead for a 256-on-128-pipeline kernel: one extra QK^T partial-softmax rescale per split (2 chunks), same PV accumulate; for Gemma-4 512 globals, 4 chunks.
performance.d256_availability: Covered under architecture.head_dims and performance.d256_feasibility: shipped in Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8, Gemma-2-9B/2.6B-class, Gemma-3 1B/4B/12B, Gemma-4 (plus 512 on Gemma-4-26B-A4B globals); absent from Llama-3/4, Mistral, Phi-4, MiniMax, GPT-OSS (64), and MLA families (v-dim 128-256 with latent compression).

design_fit.route: This item primarily informs Route A (native d=256 template for the sm_75 bridge kernel): 256 is the settled full-attention head dim of the highest-distribution open family (Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8) and Gemma-4, and cannot be reached by FA2 on sm_75 at any config. It secondarily informs Route B (k-chunked 256, extending to 512) as the fallback for the Gemma-4-26B-A4B global_head_dim 512 layers and as a lower-risk first implementation, and it bounds Route C: MLA families (DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K2/K3, GLM-5/5.2) are not served by a plain FA2-style kernel at any head dim because keys are 192-256 composed of nope+rope and the cache is a 512/576 latent - they need dedicated absorbed or split kernels regardless of the d=256 bridge.
design_fit.recommendation: Concrete target set for the sm_75 bridge kernel plan: (1) treat {64,128,256} as the mandatory native template set - 64 covers GPT-OSS, 128 covers the whole 2023-2025 installed base (Qwen2.5/3, Llama, Mistral, Phi-4, MiniMax full layers), 256 covers Qwen3-Next/3.5/3.6/3.8 full layers and Gemma-2/3/4 (the anchor workload Qwen3.8-27B: 24 heads x 256, 4 KV, 3:1 hybrid, 16 of 64 layers full); (2) make 512 reachable via the k-chunked path (2x or 4x128) specifically so Gemma-4-26B-A4B global layers can run, mirroring the FA2-for-sliding/SDPA-for-global dispatch of transformers #45201 but without the SDPA cliff; (3) do not attempt MLA in the bridge kernel - record qk 192/256 + v 128/256 + latent 512/576 as a separate kernel family; (4) key head_dim from config (explicit field), never from hidden_size/num_heads, since 10+ frontier families violate derivation. Next action: validate the d=256 template against Qwen3.8-27B full-attention layers as the correctness anchor.
design_fit.numerics_risks: Family-specific correctness hazards the kernel must honor at these dims: (1) d=256 accumulation order - QK^T over 256-wide heads doubles the FP32 accumulation chain vs 128; any k-chunked route (Route B) changes accumulation order vs a native template, so bit-exactness claims must be per-route; (2) softcap - Gemma-2/3/4 use final logit softcapping (attn_logit_softcapping; Gemma-3 softcap only on... models with softcap must apply tanh-cap before softmax; skipping it silently degrades outputs); (3) partial RoPE - Qwen3-Next/3.6/3.8 rope only the first 25% of the 256-dim head (64 dims), GLM-4.5/4.6 50%, Phi-4-mini 75%, MLA families rope exactly the 64-dim suffix - kernels assuming full-head RoPE or fusing rope at the wrong offset are wrong; (4) qk-norm - Gemma-2/3/4 and Qwen3/3.5+ apply per-head RMSNorm on Q and K, requiring pre-normalized inputs or fused norm; (5) attention sinks - GPT-OSS adds a learned per-head sink logit that must join the softmax denominator; (6) BF16 absence on sm_75/Turing (T4) while every surveyed model config declares BF16 weights (dtype bfloat16) - FP16 fallback changes numerics; (7) no documented silent wrong-output history for out-of-range dims in these families - failures are load-time errors (transformers #45201) rather than wrong results.
design_fit.demand_weighting: Who benefits from d>128 support, weighted by model distribution (HF download counts, 2026-09): Qwen is the highest-distribution open family (Qwen3.5-9B ~11.8M, Qwen3.5-4B ~7.2M, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 ~12.9M, Qwen3.8-27B ~6.2M + GGUF/MLX quantized derivatives multiplying reach) and every Qwen3.5+ full-attention layer is d=256 - so d=256 support serves the single largest serving community. Gemma-4 (26B-A4B ~8.3M, 31B ~8.3M, E4B ~4.8M downloads) adds 256 everywhere plus 512 globals. GPT-OSS gives d=64 a major installed base. d=128 remains the long tail: Llama-3/4, Mistral, Phi-4, MiniMax-M2, GLM-4.5/4.6 and all pre-2025 models keep it the highest-cumulative-install dim. MLA families (DeepSeek, Kimi-K2/K3, GLM-5) are separately weighted heavyweights (Kimi-K3 ~2.5M) but out of scope for a d=256 FA-style kernel. The SageAttention maintainer's Nov 2024 'head dim greater than 128 is quite rare' is empirically obsolete: by 2026 both of the top-two open model families by downloads ship d>128, and even diffusion serving (Ideogram 4.0) hit the 256 wall (SageAttention #47 comment, 2026-06-10).
